summary: Iteration-5 regression: full backend suite executed against freshly restarted backend. 49/49 PASS. Previously failing test_non_admin_edit_approved_resets_to_pending now passes - confirms guard at server.py:561 no longer contains the `existing.get('status','pending')=='pending'` clause, so non-admin owner (manager/center_manager/partner/accountant) can edit own approved entry and status auto-resets to 'pending' with approved_by=None.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py update_transaction guard is now correctly: `if not (is_admin or (is_owner and role in (manager, center_manager, partner, accountant)))` with separate status-reset block. Logic is clean and matches the intended approval workflow.
seed_data_creation: Tests create their own TEST_ prefixed entities/transactions and clean up via admin delete where applicable.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Full backend suite (test_finance_api.py + test_finance_features.py + test_finance_approval.py) is the regression baseline. All 49 tests pass on iteration-5. The PUT /api/transactions/{id} edit-approved-resets-to-pending fix is verified end-to-end via pytest, not just curl.
rca of the issue: Iteration-3 and Iteration-4 failure was due to an extra `existing.get('status','pending')=='pending'` clause in the guard at server.py:561 which blocked non-admin owners from editing their own approved transactions. Iteration-5: source verified to no longer contain that clause; backend restarted; pytest run confirms test_non_admin_edit_approved_resets_to_pending passes (POST as center_manager -> approve as admin -> PUT as center_manager returns 200 with status='pending', approved_by=None, amount updated).
